nodes.description: IL-11 normally signals through the membrane-bound IL-11 receptor and gp130 (classic signalling) in cranial mesenchyme around the coronal and lambdoid suture tips. In mice it is classic signalling, not trans-signalling through soluble receptor, that skull development depends on. IL-11 signalling restricts suture fusion and tooth number, so its loss removes a restraint on suture closure and on dental development. This node is the IL-11 instance of the restraint-loss entry point of the cranial suture module.

nodes.description: IL-11 promotes osteoclastogenesis directly and through osteoblast and stromal RANKL expression. Il11ra null mice have reduced osteoclast differentiation and increased trabecular bone. Keupp and colleagues proposed that loss of this osteoblast-mediated, RANKL-dependent support of osteoclast activity underlies the excess ossification at the sutures. This is a proposed mechanism, not a demonstrated one.
